newsitem.title: FRANCE: France hits back at U.S. over Africa war of words.
newsitem.headline: France hits back at U.S. over Africa war of words.

text.p: France hit back at U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher on Monday in a war of words over the role of foreign powers in Africa, insisting it had never considered the continent as its own preserve.

French Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt played down Washington's planned crisis intervention force and added pointedly that, in any case, Africans would play the main role in peacekeeping efforts.

Christopher, on his first visit to sub-Saharan Africa since taking office in 1993, indirectly accused France on Saturday of trying to maintain exclusive patronage in the region. Africa needed "the support of all its many friends, not the exclusive patronage of a few," he said.
Rummelhardt told reporters: "Every time the United States spends a dollar in Africa, we welcome this because that proves the trend towards disengagement is not progressing."
He added: "We have never considered the African continent as a French zone of influence, no more than any other region in the world is for anyone."
The U.S. plan, he said, was not new. Similar plans had been discussed by European Union heads of state in Madrid in December 1995.

"The international community will pursue discussions in Africa as well as in the relevant international bodies, and that will lead to concrete proposals for preventive diplomacy and safeguarding peace in which, in any case, the major role will be played by Africans," Rummelhardt said.
Commenting on Christopher's trip, French junior minister for cooperation Jacques Godfrain said last week that it was politically motivated ahead of the U.S. presidential election.
He said the trip followed a cut in U.S. aid for Africa and he noted that President Bill Clinton had not visited the continent during his four years in office.
